::: {#def-backpropagation}

#### Backpropagation (backprop)

**Backpropagation**, or **backprop**,
computes the [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) of a scalar, such as a loss,
with respect to every node of a [computational graph](#def-computational-graph):
it visits the nodes in the reverse of the order the forward computation made them,
and at each node applies the chain rule,
combining the gradient with respect to the node's output with the derivative of the node's own operation
[@rumelhart1986learning; @goodfellow2016deep, section 6.5].

Backpropagation is reverse-mode [automatic differentiation](pytorch-basics.qmd#def-automatic-differentiation) applied to a network's loss,
and PyTorch's `.backward()` runs it.
Some sources use "backpropagation" for the whole training algorithm, including the [parameter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) update;
these notes use it only for computing the gradient.

:::
